definitions.explanation: Describes a person who is habitually lazy and makes no effort, or such behavior. As a noun it refers to such a person. Colloquial and mildly critical in tone.

examples.japanese: {弟|おとうと}は{本当|ほんとう}にぐうたらだ。
examples.english: My little brother is really lazy.

examples.japanese: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{一日中|いちにちじゅう}ぐうたらしている。
examples.english: On my days off I laze around all day.

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい}はぐうたらだったが、{就職|しゅうしょく}してから{人|ひと}が{変|か}わったように{働|はたら}くようになった。
examples.english: He was a lazybones in his student days, but after getting a job he started working as if he were a different person.

notes:
Colloquial word for a habitually lazy person or lazy behavior. Used as a な-adjective (ぐうたらな{人|ひと}) or as a noun.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ぐうたら{者|もの}: a lazybones; good-for-nothing
- ぐうたらな{生活|せいかつ}: an idle, lazy lifestyle
- ぐうたらする: to laze around

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {怠|なま}け{者|もの}: lazy person — neutral-to-critical, more common in writing
- ものぐさ: someone who finds everything too much trouble — emphasizes not bothering rather than general idleness
